Question B-007-001-008.

Why the correct answer is right: Among those bands, the lowest frequency has the best ground-wave reach. A longer wavelength suffers less rapid ground-wave loss than the higher-frequency choices.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "40 metres": 40 metres is lower HF, but it is higher in frequency than the lowest band listed and therefore has less ground-wave reach in this comparison.
- sourceIndex 2: "10 metres": 10 metres is much higher in frequency, so it is not the band with the greatest ground-wave distance in the group.
- sourceIndex 3: "6 metres": 6 metres is VHF; ordinary coverage there is dominated by line-of-sight and special openings rather than the greatest ground-wave range.
